title: MDG Labs workflow config (.claude/workflow.json)
description: Machine-read, per-repo settings for the vendored skills, agents and scripts. Prose the agents read (area → paths, always-shared files, design-doc map) lives in the repo's CLAUDE.md '## Agent workflow' section instead.

repo.description: owner/name every gh call is scoped to.

maintainer.description: GitHub login auto-assigned to unowned issues by issue-status.yml (GitHub tracker only).

githubRunner.description: The `runs-on` value for GitHub Actions jobs setup renders (the issue-status workflow), as written in YAML: a label ("ubuntu-latest") or a label list ("[self-hosted, runners01]"). Private repos use the self-hosted runners. Default "ubuntu-latest".

ticketKey.description: Ticket prefix, e.g. RO for RO-<n>.

integration.description: Where verified work lands (e.g. dev). Equal to production in pr-per-unit repos without a dev branch.

production.description: Moves only through a PR the maintainer merges.

landing.description: dev-cherry-pick: a PASS is cherry-picked onto the integration branch and pushed. pr-per-unit: a PASS becomes its own PR against production, stacked when it depends on an unmerged one.

promotionBudget.description: Cap on reviewable files in the integration → production diff (CodeRabbit's Essentials limit is 150 files per PR, counted after path_filters); null disables the budget.

review.description: The review bots pr-review works with. A round collects the findings of every listed bot that completed a review of the PR's head, and needs at least one; a listed bot that skipped or was rate limited is reported, not treated as clean. CodeQL is not listed: pr-review reads code scanning alerts on every repository that has an analysis.

reviewers.description: Default ["kodus", "coderabbit"]. pr-review never requests a review from either; the maintainer does (`@kody start-review`, `@coderabbitai review`).

kodusConfig.description: owner/name of the org's Kodus config repo (e.g. mdg-labs/kodus-config). pr-review files there, as issues, the memories and rules Kody should learn; `gh-rest.sh kodus-config` is the only route to it. Absent: pr-review lists them in its report instead.

gate.description: The full gate: must pass before anything is pushed or lands (executor, verifier, pr-review). Per-path checks go in `checks`.

threatModel.description: Repo-relative path of the threat model security-audit and the verifier read; null when the repo has none. security-audit requires it, in the format of skills/security-audit/threat-model-format.md.

privateRepoIssues.description: While the repository is private, file every security finding, Critical and High included, as an ordinary item labelled security instead of a draft private security advisory. GitHub offers no security advisories or private vulnerability reporting on a private repository. Absent: follows the repository's visibility, so a private repository files issues. false is an error while the repository is private (security-route.sh exits 2), since GitHub offers a private repository no advisories. On a public repository findings always go to advisories, whatever this says. .claude/scripts/security-route.sh reads the visibility live and prints the result (issues or advisories). Commit messages for security fixes stay neutral either way.

securityAudit.description: security-audit settings. The review units themselves live in CLAUDE.md '### Security units'.

epic.description: Epic the file mode puts public findings under when no --epic is given: #<n> on GitHub, <KEY>-<n> on Kaneo. Absent: findings are filed with no epic.

exclude.description: Extra repo-relative globs that are not shipped source (generated code, fixtures, vendored copies), left out of the audit's coverage check on top of the generic test/generated/docs set and .coderabbit.yaml's excluded path_filters.

risk.description: Label for paths where a bug loses data (e.g. safety-critical, data-loss-risk): Opus verifier, never bundled, called out in the PR.

maintainerOnly.description: Label for work only the maintainer may run (e.g. needs-sudo); orchestrate prepares it instead of dispatching it. Maintainer-applied: gh-rest.sh refuses to add it.

spike.description: Override the spike type label name. Default spike.

requireReachableVia.description: feat/bug issues need a 'Reachable via:' acceptance criterion. Default true.

stale.description: Terms that mark an issue as written against a retired design.

exempt.description: Lines also matching this ERE are not stale (they cite the decision or negate the term).

checks.description: Checks to run when a change touches matching paths — what the executor runs before committing and the verifier re-runs under layer 1. Mirror the CI jobs those paths feed.

requires.description: Tools that must be installed (checked with command -v at the start of a run); a missing one is reported, never installed.

bootstrap.description: Command run once in every fresh scratch clone before any agent works in it (e.g. dependency install). null when none.

riskPaths.description: Globs whose changes are treated like the risk label: Opus verifier, never bundled, full risk review.

signoff.description: How commits get a DCO Signed-off-by trailer. hook: the repo's prepare-commit-msg hook adds it (clones point core.hooksPath at hooksPath); flag: git commit -s; none: no sign-off.

verifier.description: auto: sonnet, escalated to opus for risk-flagged and large-diff units. Advisory units are verified on opus under every setting. Default auto.

refiner.description: auto: sonnet, opus when any issue is risk-labelled. Default auto.

bundle.description: Max items per executor dispatch. Default 3.

attempts.description: Fix attempts before asking, unless findings keep narrowing. Default 3.

rebaseRetries.description: Re-runs after a landing conflict. Default 2.

growth.description: Pulled-in items allowed before asking. Default 3.

confirmAbove.description: Confirm the plan with the maintainer above this many items. Default 12.

inSessionFindings.description: pr-review fixes a round in-session when it has at most this many small, non-risk findings; otherwise it delegates to executor/verifier agents. Default 5.

lines.description: Changed lines (generated code excluded) above which the verifier is Opus under models.verifier auto, and the report names the item. Default 2000.

act.description: Lets the executor and verifier run the GitHub Actions jobs a unit changes locally with nektos/act, through .claude/scripts/act-run.sh. null disables it (changed workflows are then judged by reading them, plus actionlint).

platforms.description: runs-on label → container image, passed to act as -P. Name every label the repo's workflows use, e.g. ubuntu-latest and runners01.

neverRun.description: Job-id globs never run locally, also when another job needs them: deploys, migrations, releases, publishing, secret syncs.

timeout.description: Seconds for one run, and for waiting on another lane's run. Default 1800.

branchPrefix.description: Default agent/. A unit's branch is <prefix><unit-id>.

landingRepos.description: Sibling repositories an item may land in, selected by a 'Lands in: owner/repo' line in its body. The item stays tracked here; its commit closes it with 'Fixes <repo>#n'.

pathEnv.description: Env var holding the local clone path.

defaultPath.description: Path relative to this repo when the env var is unset.

postVerdict.description: Whether verifiers post their verdict comment on items landing here. false for routine items (e.g. template bumps) where a long verdict is noise; the verdict then goes to the orchestrator only. Default true.

unitEnvironment.description: A per-unit isolated environment (e.g. a loop-device lab) agents must start under the unit id and destroy before reporting.

idVar.description: Env var carrying the unit id, e.g. HOSERVA_LAB_ID.

teardown.description: Command, run in the clone, that destroys the unit's environment. {UNIT} is replaced by the unit id.

leftoverCheck.description: Command that prints nothing when no environment is left behind. {UNIT} is replaced by the unit id.

docs.description: Public docs pages that have their own writing guide.

guide.description: Repo-relative path of the skill/guide agents read before writing a page.

maintainerApplied.description: Only the maintainer applies this label, because a CI gate or a skill reads it as the maintainer's approval (e.g. migration:contract). gh-rest.sh issue-create and issue-edit refuse to add it; removing it stays possible. A guard against accidents, not a security boundary: an agent calling the API directly with the same credential can still apply it.
